articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators' (Digest No.115)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
abstract: The multi-wavelength transport network project is looking at the provision of an optical extension layer for the existing network. This optical transport layer would provide a broadband network, transparent to varying data formats and capable of operating at high bit rates. Network nodes in the uppermost layer could provide optical cross-connect and a local add/drop function in the wavelength domain, while switching of data takes place electronically at the lower levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A joint European demonstration of fibre in the loop: RACE projects R1030 ACCESS and R2014 FIRST
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
abstract: The RACE project ACCESS had the main goal of defining a fibre based Customer Access Connection (CAC) for residential and small business users which can be deployed cost effectively from the mid'nineties. The project started in 1988 with the assumption that users initially would require 622 Mbit/s of bandwidth provided by one fibre between the exchange and each user. It was redirected towards a double star passive optical network concept with the assumption that initial service requirement is TV distribution and teleservices up to 2 Mbit/s. It concluded in 1992 by giving recommendations for CAC implementations and many of these are now adopted in large scale implementations. The FIRST project is using recommendations and technologies developed in ACCESS and elsewhere and applying them in a field trial. The practical system application will give important information about technologies and system requirements vital for the economical deployment of optical CACs. Issues include standardised 2Mbit/s interface to the exchange, management system requirements, reliability, operation and maintenance, digital and analogue TV transmission and life cycle cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RACE 1051: demonstration of a multigigabit technology for provision of digital video services
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
abstract: Within the RACE project 1051 'Multigigabit Transmission in the IBCN Subscriber Loop' the major technologies for 5 and 10 Gbit/s fibre-optic transmission systems have been developed and tested in system demonstrators. Components and building blocks for all system functions such as multiplexer, laser driver, receiver preamplifier, main amplifier, regenerator and demultiplexer/channel selector have been realized in the form of Sil bipolar chips for both bit rates. Integrated transmitter and receiver modules have been built around advanced optoelectronic components. With a cascade of four optical amplifiers it was possible to bridge a budget of 100 dB at 10 Gbit/s without applying optical filters. This means that more than eight million customers can be supplied by only one optical transmitter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
abstract: RACE Project 1036 has developed a Broadband Customer Premises Network to the point where a test bed could be demonstrated whose performance was representative of what could be achieved by production components. The network uses wavelength and time division multiplexing (WTDM) to give a total capacity on a single bearer of over 38 Gbit/s. Features include close wavelength spacing (4 nm), high-speed time multiplexing (2.48 Gbit/s), and a layered control protocol. The WTDM system is based on a network of local routeing centres each serving a number of sources and destinations. Combining both wavelength and time-division multiplexing in this way extends network capacities considerably, without stretching either technique beyond what can be demonstrated in a practical system within RACE timescales.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RACE project 2012 HIPOS 40 Gbit/s OTDM transmission systems with optical demultiplexers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
abstract: This paper pays particular attention to the 40 Gbit/s test bed developed to assess the performance of the polymer demultiplexer. In addition to the basic performance of the testbed, the requirement of satisfactory performance for all transmitted channels, rather than just a single channel, and the start-up difficulties involved in demodulating this signal down to the base rate (for example 10 Gbit/s) are discussed. Transmission of a single polarisation 'true' 40 Gbit/s OTDM data stream over 205 km using a stabilised 10 GHz erbium fibre ring laser and four independently driven lithium niobate modulators to generate the signal, and a 40 GHz electronic clock recovery circuit to drive the lithium niobate demultiplexer array with 10 GHz sine waves, is demonstrated. An outline of the remainder of the project is given, including materials and fabrication issues.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The RACE programme-an overview of the key role of optical technology
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
abstract: The RACE optical technology demonstrators constitute a set of important milestones along the development path to an economic optical telecommunications infrastructure. They provide a realistic test for new concepts and components, and pave the way towards more extensive field trials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
abstract: This fully engineered demonstrator examines the application of coherent multichannel techniques to broadband signal distribution (e.g. television and high-definition television) in the local loop. Ten 140 Mbit/s digitised video signals are transmitted on ten optical carriers 10 GHz apart. Up to 1000 receiver terminals can be served from a single central transmitter assembly. The paper explores the system operation, system specifications and subsystem results achieved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical routing for future broadcaster requirements-RACE 2001
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on RACE Optical Systems and Demonstrators
abstract: The RACE 2001 programme follows on from the RACE 1036 programme to take the developed and proven technology and apply it to a commercially viable Wavelength and Time Division Multiplexed application. This paper describes how those original ambitions have been addressed, what new considerations were necessary and what success has been achieved on the project.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
